narration.text: If Jupiter vanished, why wouldn't Earth notice?
It outweighs every other planet combined.
About 2.5 times all the others together.
Yet it's under one-thousandth of the Sun's mass.
So Earth's orbit would barely change at first.
The Sun's small wobble around Jupiter would fade.
Asteroid and comet orbits would slowly rearrange over ages.
So the loss is felt in deep time, not tomorrow.
